jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral positions and DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowship at the Cosmic Dawn Center
jobs.description:
The Cosmic Dawn Center (DAWN) invites applications for both the DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowship and postdoctoral positions to work on specific projects.

  DAWN is a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation (DNRF) and is located in the Copenhagen area at the Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen and the Space division of the Danish Technical University (DTU-Space). In addition, DAWN has several associates at major research institutes across Europe, North America, and Australia. DAWN brings together experts in all aspects of early Universe research and is deeply involved in major existing and upcoming surveys with JWST and HST (e.g. SPURS, COSMOS3D, FRESCO, COSMOS-Web, RUBIES, BEACON, and CLUTCH), ALMA (e.g. CHAMPS), and Euclid (e.g. Cosmic Dawn Survey of the deep fields), as well as simulations. 

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowships

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowships are intended for outstanding scientists whose research falls within DAWN’s research themes focused on the early Universe: first stars, high-redshift galaxy evolution, reionization and evolution of the IGM, high-redshift transients and supernovae, dust and ISM in the early Universe, massive galaxy evolution, and dark matter. DAWN Postdoctoral Fellows are expected to pursue their own independent, cutting-edge research programs in collaboration with DAWN members.

  Postdoctoral positions

  Up to two postdoctoral position are available as part of the DFF Sapere Aude-funded project “Revealing Massive Stars at Cosmic Dawn” in Associate Professor Charlotte Mason’s group at DAWN/NBI to work on both observational and theoretical projects on galaxy formation and reionization, with a particular focus on JWST spectroscopy from the SPURS survey. Applicants with interests and expertise in any of galaxy formation, stellar populations, Lyman-alpha emission, IGM/CGM evolution, galaxy-dark matter connections at high redshift, JWST NIRSpec spectroscopy, statistical inference and comparing hydrodynamical simulations to observations are strongly encouraged to apply.

  Additional postdoctoral positions may be available to work on specific projects at DAWN funded through individual group leadership grants. Applicants with research interests in any of the above DAWN research themes are strongly encouraged to apply. 

  Applicants to this position will be automatically considered for all available postdoctoral and Postdoctoral Fellowship positions at DAWN/NBI. We note a separation application is required for applications to the positions at DAWN/DTU in the group of Associate Professor Kasper Heintz.

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellows and postdocs are encouraged to collaborate with DAWN’s international associates, and have the opportunity to supervise students and to apply for grants and observing proposals as PI. More information on DAWN’s activities and researchers is available at https://cosmicdawn.dk.

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowships and postdoc positions are for up to three years. The employment can start as early as Spring 2027 or upon agreement with the chosen candidate.

  Further information on the Department is linked at http://www.science.ku.dk/english/about-the-faculty/organisation/. Inquiries about the positions can be made to Associate Professor Charlotte Mason charlotte.mason@nbi.ku.dk.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff. Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellows and postdocs receive generous support for computing, travel and publication expenses. Most non-Danish citizens are eligible for a favorable tax scheme. Copenhagen is a beautiful, family-friendly city with a large international community, a lively and diverse cultural scene, and a very high quality of life. We offer an attractive starting salary plus pension and negotiation for a salary supplement is possible. Benefits include six weeks paid vacation and generous benefits including: pension, full health cover (also for family), paid sick leave and paid parental leave. More on employment conditions and living in Copenhagen: http://ism.ku.dk. 

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Cover letter – maximum 1 page, describing your motivation for applying to DAWN 	
• Research plan – maximum 3 pages including figures and references, description of current and future research plans 	
• Curriculum vitae, including a list of up to 3 people who could be contacted for references 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree, if applicable, or equivalent – a letter from your university/supervisor stating you have completed requirements for these degrees and are in the final year of a PhD is fine) 	
• Publication list   The deadline for applications is 6 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarships in Economics at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for one fully funded PhD scholarship at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark. The position is based at SDU’s Esbjerg campus.

The successful candidate will be enrolled in the 5+3 PhD programme. The programme includes a research stay abroad, typically of six months’ duration, and offers a competitive full-time salary.

We aim to appoint the successful candidate as soon as possible, ideally with a start date of 15 January 2027, while remaining flexible regarding the exact timing.

About the Department and Research Environment

The Department of Economics is an international department with a strong tradition of excellence in research and teaching across a wide range of fields within economics. Research, teaching, and outreach activities are organized within five research groups: Econometrics and Data Science; Economic History; Macroeconomics; Microeconomics; and Environmental and Resource Economics. Further information about the department and its research groups is available on the department website.

The PhD student will be affiliated with the Environmental and Resource Economics (ERE) group, which focuses on Environmental and Natural resource economics on a variety of topics, namely ecosystem conservation and use, marine resource use, management and conservation, energy transitions, climate regulation, and interdisciplinary research at the interface between economics and the natural sciences. The group applies economic theory and tools to policy and analysis to provide guidance for more efficient use of environmental and natural resource goods and services.

The position

The successful candidate will become part of an international research environment and work closely with Associate Professors Ana Faria Lopes and Melina Kourantidou.  Part of the work will contribute to the BRAVE (Biological Invasions Resolved through Adaptable, Versatile, and Engaging Nature-Based Solutions) project, a Biodiversa+ -funded project that investigates the complex ecological and societal challenges associated with invasive species and their management. In particular, the research will contribute to the Danish BRAVE case study on the invasive Pacific oyster in the Wadden Sea, including work on stakeholder preferences, economic values, and trade-offs associated with its management. For further information about the project, please see this link or this link.

The project relies on the application of economic theories, namely non-market valuation and bioeconomic modelling, to investigate the management of invasive species. We welcome candidates with strong quantitative and analytical skills from economics or related disciplines, including candidates with interdisciplinary backgrounds and an interest in environmental and resource management.  There will be considerable scope for the PhD student to develop their own research questions within the broader themes of the project.

The successful candidate is expected to contribute to high-quality research within the scope of the project, through both collaborative research and independent work, including a single-authored paper. In addition, the candidate will be involved in teaching and supervision within economics at both undergraduate and graduate levels.

The PhD student will be supervised by Associate Professor Ana Faria Lopes as the main supervisor and will join a research group that includes postdoctoral researcher and research assistants, with access to an international network of collaborators.

Applicants’ profile

Applicants should have completed a relevant master’s degree in Environmental and Resource Management, Economics, Mathematics and Economics, or related disciplines. Furthermore, we expect applicants to:

• 
Have solid quantitative and analytical skills, with experience in data analysis and applied quantitative methods using R, Stata, or similar tools, and be eager to learn and apply new methods.

• 
Be dedicated, capable of working independently and collaboratively as part of a research team.

• 
Have strong English skills, both spoken and written. 

• 
Have willingness to participate in stakeholder engagement activities and communicate research findings to different audiences. 

• 
Have good interpersonal skills, be interested in engaging with national and international researchers.

The following qualifications are an advantage

• 
Have an interest in, or potentially experience with, non-market valuation, press analysis, GIS and/or bioeconomic modelling.

• 
Experience conducting empirical research.

• 
Demonstrated interest in environmental and resource economics.

• 
Knowledge of Danish or another Scandinavian language would be an advantage for stakeholder engagement and work with locally relevant material but is not a requirement.

We are an international department, and the working language is English.

Further information about the position can be obtained from Head of Administration Astrid Holm Nielsen, e-mail: astni@sam.sdu.dk. For general questions regarding relocation, housing, taxes etc., contact the SDU’s International Staff Office. 

How to apply for this position

Employment as a paid PhD fellow takes place in accordance with the circular of 20 December 2021 on the collective agreement for academics in the state – appendix 5, protocol on PhD fellowships.

For more information on the department guidelines for qualification and recruitment please see our Appointment Guidelines.

The application must include (all attachments must be in Adobe PDF format): 

• 
Detailed CV - the education and work history must be month and year specific.

• 
A certified copy of your master’s degree certificate, including transcripts of all examination results.  Foreign diplomas that are not in Norwegian, Swedish or English must be accompanied by a translation into Danish or English, as well as a translation of the official description of the marking scale used.

• 
A motivational letter describing why the applicant is a good match for analyzing the topic and how the applicant’s skills provide a solid foundation to do so (max. 5 pages incl. reference list).

• 
A project description (max 5 pages of 2400 characters each, including spaces, notes, appendices, bibliography etc.).

• 
When applying for a PhD scholarship, please fill in the application form available on our web page. 

On the webpage of the PhD-school, you can find the guidelines for preparing your project proposal.

All non-Danish documents must be translated into English.

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material.

Once the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicant will receive the portion of the evaluation that pertains to them.

Applications that are incomplete regarding the above requirements will not be assessed by the committee.

Shortlisting and tests may be used in the assessment process.

As part of the overall assessment of the applicant’s qualifications, an interview may be applied.

Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

The application and CV must not exceed 10 MB.

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, 23.59 CET/CEST.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website. Uploaded files must be in Adobe PDF (unlocked) or Word format.

We recommend that you read the guideline for applicants. If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk before the application deadline.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

Salary and employment terms

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

proprty.ai is building a service to help Danish property managers leverage machine learning technology to create better condition assessments and maintenance plans. The cost of maintaining the Danish property mass is growing fast, and property managers are struggling to keep up with maintenance and regulatory responsibilities. This is not only hurting the property managers, but also the people using and living in the buildings. The challenge to live up to the EU Taxonomy for Sustainable Activities, is made harder, by not having the tools nor data to make the right strategic choices when planning and executing maintenance. With our service we aim to create property condition assessment and maintenance plans faster and more accurately than what is possible today. Using machine learning algorithms trained on millions of m2 worth of data, we can provide property managers with data to make the right decisions, when it comes to spending resources on maintenance. That way they can cut costs, improve property conditions and push the property mass towards a sustainable future. We're creating an AI powered web platform, that allows property managers to create condition assessments and maintenance plans in a fraction of the time they're using today, by mixing output from our machine learning models with boots on the ground input. It's not only faster. It provides high quality data instead of subjective information. At proprty.ai we've already signed partnerships with 18% of the Danish residential property market. We have a very real problem to solve, and a strong team to do it.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in High-Speed Hyperspectral and Super-Resolution Terahertz Imaging - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
Are you interested in pushing terahertz (THz) imaging beyond today’s limits in speed, bandwidth, and spatial resolution? 

At DTU Electro, you will work at the interface of ultrafast THz photonics, nonlinear optical detection, coherent imaging, and machine learning to develop a new generation of high-speed hyperspectral THz imaging technology.

The PhD project is part of the DFF-funded INSPIRING project (High-speed hyperspectral and super-resolution terahertz imaging). INSPIRING will combine broadband THz-to-near-infrared upconversion with CMOS-array detection to enable high-speed THz imaging. Your main role will be to establish the imaging platform and develop hyperspectral and machine-learning methods for super-resolution imaging and material identification.

You will work in an international, interdisciplinary team at DTU Electro. The project includes a planned 3–6-month research stay in Prof. Xi-Cheng Zhang’s group at the University of Rochester, USA.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your research will focus on high-speed coherent THz imaging with machine learning. 

You will:

• Develop and operate a broadband coherent THz imaging platform using optical rectification and/or laser-induced plasma THz sources.
• Implement wide-field imaging based on THz-to-NIR upconversion and CMOS focal-plane-array detection.
• Acquire and analyze time-domain hyperspectral THz data with a target bandwidth above 10 THz.
• Apply machine-learning methods, including CNN and autoencoder-type architectures, for super-resolution reconstruction and material identification.
• Study semiconductors, polymers, multilayer structures, and industrial test samples, and collaborate with project partners in Denmark and abroad. 
• Publish your results in peer-reviewed journals and present them at international conferences.
We are looking for a highly motivated and curious candidate with a strong background in experimental photonics, optics, applied physics, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. Experience with THz spectroscopy, ultrafast laser systems, nonlinear optics, or optical imaging is highly desirable. Experience with scientific programming, data analysis, image processing, or machine learning will be considered an advantage. You should have a strong interest in experimental research and be comfortable working with complex optical setups as well as analyzing large multidimensional datasets. We value creativity, independent problem-solving, and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment. You should also have good communication skills and be able to present and communicate your scientific results clearly in written and spoken English.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Associate Professor Binbin Zhou, Professor Peter Uhd Jepsen, and Associate Professor Francesco Da Ros. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The start date is 1 January 2027 (or by mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Binbin Zhou at zhou@dtu.dk. 

You can read more about DTU Electro at www.electro.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro  
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Picture your typical week: on Monday you’re on-site at a pharmaceutical client, leading a cross-functional team through a critical MES go-live. By Wednesday you’re working with the IT leadership to turn your delivery results into a business case for the next phase. Friday, you’re back at Emendo’s Nordhavn office sharing what you learned and sharpening the methods your colleagues will use on their projects. If that sounds like work you’d love, keep reading.

Why We’re Hiring Now

We paused hiring over the past year to be deliberate about the team we build next. The consulting market in Denmark has tightened, and our clients have changed how they buy: they want fewer consultants with more experience, people who can walk into a complex situation and show measurable progress within weeks, not months. We are now making a small number of senior hires — each one matters, and we are taking the time to find the right people.

About Emendo

Emendo is a 200-person consultancy built by people who used to sit on the client side — running transformation programmes inside pharma before deciding to do it for a living. We understand the pressure a site director feels before a go-live, we know what an inspector looks for, and we speak the language of the people who operate the systems we implement. We work across the full pharmaceutical value chain from R&D through shipping, with offices in Copenhagen, Kalundborg, Odense, Silkeborg, Munich, and Raleigh (USA). Our strategy is simple: deliver faster, prove value in hard numbers, and use our methods and AI tools to do what we do well — only quicker.

We are a methods-driven firm rooted in operational excellence and Lean. Our motto, Observe, Think, Improve, is itself a method: go to the floor, understand what is actually happening, analyse it rigorously, then design and implement a concrete improvement. That simplicity is what makes it reliable when the project gets complicated and the usual playbooks stop working.

The Role

You will lead IT/OT transformation engagements for clients in pharma and regulated industries — operating at the intersection of technology, business process, and organisational change. You are expected to create measurable impact from the outset, build trusted relationships with client stakeholders, and identify opportunities to expand Emendo’s footprint within your accounts. At Emendo, seniority means more than years served: it means sound judgement in ambiguity, credibility with demanding stakeholders, and the willingness to raise the standard of the whole team.

What You Will Do

• Lead client engagements on-site, owning delivery of IT/OT implementations across enterprise, operations management, process control, and process equipment layers

• Drive measurable progress in short cycles — the kind your client’s leadership can point to in a steering committee: cost reduced, lead time shortened, risk closed out

• Manage project governance, solution architecture alignment, and validation concepts within complex, multi-stakeholder environments

• Shape how Emendo works — contribute to our methods, package what you learn into repeatable offerings and case studies, and use AI tools to deliver faster without cutting corners

• Build lasting client relationships — become a trusted partner to your stakeholders, spot opportunities for follow-on work, and contribute to Emendo’s business development by turning strong delivery into new engagements

• Apply Observe, Think, Improve as your foundation — and mentor junior colleagues to do the same

What It Takes

Must-Have Qualifications

• Master’s degree in engineering, IT, or a related discipline

• 6–10+ years of hands-on delivery experience in IT/OT project management, product ownership, or solution implementation — ideally within pharma or other regulated industries, though strong candidates from adjacent sectors are welcome

• Track record of delivering quantifiable business outcomes (cost reduction, lead-time improvement, risk mitigation) — not just on-time/on-budget projects

• Strong command of project governance, stakeholder management, and the ability to engage credibly with C-suite and senior client leadership

• Deep understanding of at least one area: enterprise systems (ERP/MES), process control, IT–OT convergence, or value chain technology

• Fluent English, both written and spoken; Danish skills are strongly preferred, or a commitment to learn

• Willingness to work on-site at client locations in Denmark and occasionally internationally

Nice to have — but not required

None of the following are dealbreakers. If you tick even one or two, it tells us you will ramp up faster — but we have seen great consultants arrive without any of them and build the expertise here.

• Experience with GxP compliance, computer system validation (CSV/CSA), or regulatory frameworks in life sciences

• Familiarity with AI/automation tools applied to enterprise transformation or operational settings

• Background in operational excellence, Lean, or continuous improvement methodologies

• Experience working across multiple sites or geographies in global transformation programmes

• Comfort with outcome-based or fixed-price engagement models

What Makes Emendo Different

• Measured on outcomes, not utilisation — you work directly with industry leaders on engagements that matter

• One integrated firm with deep methods: cross-unit collaboration across Implementation, Engineering, Digital, and R&D, backed by a Lean toolbox and AI accelerators

• Freedom under responsibility — challenging projects with room to shape the solution and your own career

• A flat culture where your input matters and your wins are celebrated

• Competitive compensation reflecting the seniority and impact expected in this role

This role is probably not for you if:

• You prefer purely advisory work with limited implementation responsibility.

• You work best with narrow ownership and very clear boundaries.

• You have strong technical exposure but limited experience leading cross-functional change.

Ready to Make an Impact?

We are hiring two to three Senior Consultants this year. Each one joins a team that has led some of the largest IT/OT programmes in US and European pharma — people who chose Emendo because they wanted senior-level impact in a firm that still feels personal. If that resonates, we’d like to hear from you.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. We will be in touch promptly.

For further information, reach out to Mikael Elley (me@emendo.com or +45 24 83 62 01).

Building AI keeps getting cheaper and faster. Deciding what's worth building, and getting an organisation to actually commit to it, does not.

At Heyra, we build AI systems, workflows and data platforms that are meant to live in production from day one. We work closely with companies that are moving quickly and need a partner who can hold both the strategic picture and the delivery reality in one head.

We're looking for a Deployment Strategist: the person the client's leadership talks to. You own the relationship and the outcome. You sit with a C-suite buyer, understand where their business is actually trying to go, and translate that into a sharp, sequenced plan for what we build and why. Then you steer a strong engineering team to make it real - without being the one in the codebase.

This is the strategic counterpart to our engineers. Where they go deep into the build, you hold the commercial and strategic frame: what problem are we really solving, what impact are we creating, in what order, and how do we get the organisation to adopt it. You're more product manager than a traditional consultant, with a strong strategic angle - closer to an Engagement Manager who's technical enough to make the right calls than a slide-deck advisor.

You'll work closely with engineers, data specialists, strategists and designers in a company where ideas move quickly and the distance from thinking to building is intentionally small.

What you'll work on

• 
Owning client relationships at the leadership level - being the person the C-suite trusts

• 
Framing the real problem behind the ask, and shaping it into an engagement worth running together with our FDEs

• 
Sequencing what gets built, in what order, and being accountable for the business value - not just the artifact

• 
Steering engineering teams toward outcomes, translating in both directions between the client and the builders

• 
Driving adoption: managing expectations, working with the people who have to live with the solution, and staying through the part after launch

• 
Scoping, structuring and de-risking engagements as they evolve

• 
Spotting where the next opportunity sits inside an account and growing it

Requirements

You probably have experience with

• 
Management consulting, change management, adoption, implementation of AI-native solutions.

• 
Owning client or stakeholder relationships end to end, with real accountability for outcomes

• 
Product, programme or engagement leadership in a technical environment

• 
Being technically literate - fluent enough in data and AI to make the right calls and earn trust with both buyers and builders, without needing to write the production code yourself

• 
Translating between business strategy and what's actually buildable

• 
Bringing structure to ambiguous, fast-moving situations

• 
The patience to sit with a worried manager, and the stubbornness to stay until adoption actually lands

Curiosity, taste and the way you think matter just as much to us as specific tools or years of experience. We hire for the who, not the what - experience is an indicator of perspective, not a deciding factor for how senior a role you'll play here. We're hiring across levels and shape the role around the person.

Why Heyra

At Heyra, we believe consulting needs to be rewritten. We're building a consultancy designed for the agentic era. We design, build, and operate AI products that change how enterprises work - from problem to prototype to production.

We care deeply about craft, speed and building things that work in the real world.

Heyra brings together people from engineering, strategy, product, startup and creative environments. We keep teams small, collaboration close and momentum high.

You'll join a team where:

people care deeply about what they build

good ideas move quickly

new technology gets explored early

and where there is room to shape both the company and the way we work
